title: 29 U.S.C. § 1109 — Liability for Breach of Fiduciary Duty
built_by: Claude (assistant) under direction of Michael Hartmann

evolution_stages.key_change: Personal liability rule enacted; trust-law fiduciary standard adopted; functional definition of fiduciary
§ 1109(c) added: exemptions do not shield from § 1109 liability; core (a) text unchanged

case_law.rule: § 1109 duty of prudence includes ongoing monitoring obligation; fiduciary must periodically review investment options, not just select them at a point in time; limitations period runs from breach of monitoring duty, not initial selection
No presumption of prudence for any ERISA fiduciary; objective prudent-expert standard applies to all decisions; no Moench presumption; plausible complaint standard for § 1109 claims

primary_application.breach_theory: Plan administrator processed unauthorized retirement election for active 44-year-old participant without adequate identity verification, in breach of the prudent-expert standard under § 1104(a)(1)(B). No prudent plan administrator familiar with identity fraud against benefit systems would process a sub-normal-retirement-age election without identity verification.
loss_categories: Benefit payments made to fraudulent claimant under unauthorized election
Accrual credit lost during period fraudulent election was in effect
primary_application.relief_sought: § 1132(a)(2): plan made whole; unauthorized election rescinded; fiduciary removal available if administrator was complicit

dol_anchor.description: DOL Cybersecurity Program Best Practices (April 2021) defines standard of care for plan fiduciaries on identity verification. Relevant guidance: 'Implement strong access controls' including authentication practices for benefit elections. While not binding, DOL guidance defines the prudent-expert standard's current floor.
